purpose: Use surviving-object evidence as a reverse index to close existing UK, narrowly UK-linked US, and already-open European historical-source chains. Do not resume geographic discovery for coverage.
authority_note: For live task status consult data/analysis/CURRENT_STATE.json and data/analysis/global_archive_research_priority_CURRENT.json. This file preserves the object-to-corpus chain summaries.

scope.core: United Kingdom nineteenth-century slide preparation, circulation, commerce, teaching, comparison, material publication, and surviving-object provenance.
scope.secondary: United States only where an already-open British reception/exchange/object chain exists.
scope.europe: Existing continental-European chains may be closed when already present in the corpus/object layer; do not open new national infrastructures.
scope.parked: Further non-UK/US/Europe geographic expansion for completeness.
scope.bibliography_state: slide-locked-pass-19; 206 verified entries. Passes 18-19 remain audit history and are not the active frontier.
scope.frozen_object_survey_state: 307 discovery nodes / 155 strict nineteenth-century nodes; CLOSED_2026-08-09

working_model.historical_corpus: journals, catalogues, advertisements, correspondence, society proceedings, manuals and period texts
working_model.github_object_layer: surviving-object reverse index: labels, series numbers, cabinet positions, accessions, cards, catalogues and present custody
working_model.closure_rule: Prefer a bounded historical relation that removes an open edge over another collection discovery. Modern museum prose remains object metadata/evidence, not nineteenth-century corpus text.

closure_status.target: Arthur C. Cole, Studies in Microscopical Science, vols. I-II
closure_status.result: Full local OCR structured; volume architecture, numbered studies, plate counts, role division and volume-specific preparation responsibility closed. Vol. I credits Martin J. Cole; Vol. II credits Martin J. Cole and Arthur C. Cole jointly.
closure_status.next: Later vols III-IV only if a writing question requires them.

closure_status.target: Charles Collins Jr., Fish Scales / Special Micro-Slides
closure_status.result: 1884 48-species Fish Scales notice, 1885 expanded Special Micro-Slides repertoire, and St Andrews surviving Collins fish skin/scales group form a closed series-level chain.
closure_status.next: Whole Microscopical News IV ingestion is optional context, not a closure requirement.

closure_status.target: H. L. Smith, Diatomacearum Species Typicae, Century III
closure_status.result: Surviving architecture fixes Century III at nos. 201-300; UK reception closes Century I packaging/address system and Century II receipt.
closure_status.next: Recover exact 1878 Century III notice/pages only if reception chronology is needed.

closure_status.target: Frederic Kitton, Norfolk Diatoms Series III-IV
closure_status.result: Surviving Farlow series explicitly gives I-IV, nos.1-100, 25 numbers each; Series III=51-75 and IV=76-100.
closure_status.next: Contemporary III-IV prospectus optional for distribution chronology.

closure_status.target: John Thomas Norman 1862 exhibition / 1872 catalogue / St Andrews group
closure_status.result: Collection-level chain closes public exhibition, 2,584-mount catalogue scale and surviving institutional group.
closure_status.next: Wait for a complete St Andrews Norman item/export layer before row-by-row catalogue matching.

closure_status.target: Andrew Pritchard 1835 preparation catalogue / surviving cases
closure_status.result: Corrected old 1837 error: preparation-list target is 1835. Contemporary surviving case and later Whipple catalogue-labelled mixed cabinet close the object bridge; 1842 provides later catalogue state.
Official 4,723 dataset records versus 4,713 physical containers/objects kept separate; diagnostic preparation/address architecture already structured.
closure_status.next: Full no-early-exit XLSX harvest when the binary is retrievable.

closure_status.target: Charles Elcock St Andrews Challenger letters ms21974-ms21975
closure_status.result: Exact two-letter locator closed; catalogue explicitly records Challenger-sample references within broader antiquarian/natural-history correspondence.

closure_status.target: Naples catalogue offering 383 ↔ St Andrews BPM/1/T8/6
closure_status.result: Local primary catalogue OCR recovers row 383 as Delphinus phocaena L., Penis by ditto continuation from row 382. The surviving St Andrews slide carries Stazione Zoologica Napoli labels, the taxon Delphinus phocaena and right-label transcription 'Panis 383'. Station + taxon + exact catalogue number close the correspondence to offering 383.
closure_status.guard: Preserve the source discrepancy 'Penis' versus St Andrews transcription 'Panis'. Offering correspondence does not prove individual manufacturing date, preparator, price or identity with a particular shipment copy.
closure_status.next: No active search. Reopen only if object photography or production/shipment records are needed for a specific argument.

new_knowledge_from_crosswalk.result: Slides accumulate maker, series, cabinet, society, accession and database addresses; re-addressing and retrieval are historical processes.
Postal circuits join slides to manuscript books, notes, drawings, packing, postage, damage liability and valuation.
Commercially identified preparations could later function as reference/test objects for objective comparison.
Cole-style synchronized preparation+text+plate issues, Type Slides, ordinary catalogue commodities, replicated sets and anatomical serial sections remain distinct forms.

stop_rules: Do not continue global bibliography expansion for coverage alone.
Do not build new non-UK/US/Europe collection infrastructure at the current project stage.
Do not open broad US microscopy harvesting; follow only already-open UK-linked chains.
Do not bulk-ingest modern museum prose into the nineteenth-century corpus.
Do not open new medium domains such as geological thin sections without a separate scope decision.
When a chain reaches collection/series architecture sufficient for argument, downgrade residual prospectus/page hunting to optional unless it changes attribution, chronology or object identity.
Do not repeat public-web searching for the four request-only residuals unless a new bounded identifier appears.
